sources.entry: ScreenCat - ScreenCat is a screen sharing + remote collaboration application.

summary.one_liner: ScreenCat is an alpha-stage, open source (BSD) desktop screen sharing app that also lets a remote person control your mouse and keyboard.
summary.what_it_does: ScreenCat shares the host computer's entire desktop over a WebRTC video channel using Chromium's experimental chromeMediaSource 'screen' feature. The remote viewer can send mousedown and keydown events over a WebRTC data channel, and the host synthesizes those inputs with robotjs. A remote user can join through a normal browser via a remote control page, or two ScreenCat.app users can connect to each other. Connection setup uses cat-lobby, a minimal HTTP and Server-Sent Events server that swaps SDP payloads so users don't copy/paste them. The app is written in JS, HTML and CSS (with tachyons CSS) and wrapped in Electron using the menubar module. The README says it works best between Macs, and can also be built for Linux or Windows.
use_cases: share my desktop with a remote collaborator
remote control someone's computer from a browser
open source alternative to commercial screen sharing
notable: Remote viewers can join from a normal browser (Google Chrome recommended) with no install needed
Uses Chromium's experimental chromeMediaSource 'screen' WebRTC feature to capture the full desktop
Signaling handled by cat-lobby, a small HTTP and Server-Sent Events lobby server
Only native component is a robotjs-based C++ addon for synthesizing mouse and keyboard events
caveats: Alpha status, aimed at developers and early adopters; the README says it is not as good as commercial alternatives
Builds for every OS may not be available, so you may need to build it yourself
Windows build requires Visual Studio C++ to compile native modules
